scenes.text: Shoppers look around, pick things up, and then they're gone. Most shops never find out why. Meet Leo. He runs a small furniture shop in a busy city. Every day, shoppers walk by, browse a little, and leave. Leo has clues: what they looked at, what they almost bought, and how they paid. But those clues live in different places, so every campaign is a guess. Who should he reach? And what should he offer?

scenes.text: So, could AI help Leo decide? Meet Market Metro: a living, simulated city where AI agents observe shoppers, train models and test marketing campaigns. Then we measure what changed: purchases, merchant contribution and PayPal payment outcomes.

scenes.text: First, the data needs meaning. Our ontology connects shoppers, products, contacts and payments, so every prediction learns from the right examples. Recommendations and inquiries never get mixed up. And one strict rule: earlier signals can be inputs, but later outcomes are kept for labels and evaluation.

scenes.text: Now the planner agent gets to work. It studies demand and available stock, picks twenty eight days of history, and asks local tools to train two candidate models. Every decision, tool call and result becomes a checkpoint you can open.

scenes.text: But nothing ships on a hunch. The verifier tests both models in matching development markets, checking PayPal and merchant outcomes side by side. Only a tested winner is published; otherwise, the current policy stays.
